content:
Megyn Kelly did not pull any punches during her brutal criticism of Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) on Monday, when she called the Democratic lawmaker a “nutcase,” following a tense interview with CNN over why she suddenly decided to endorse a Trump-backed candidate for Michigan.

Stevens faces major criticism from her own party following an eleventh-hour endorsement of Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers, who she once warned would “keep rubber-stamping Donald Trump’s harmful agenda.”

The lawmaker appeared on CNN on Sunday but struggled to explain why she endorsed Rogers after aggressively backing Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed, whom she lost to in the primary election. However, she told Anderson Cooper that El-Sayed is “getting angrier and angrier.”

“Look, this is just a weight off my shoulders, OK. Abdul has been getting angrier and angrier. I was trying to help, and I endorsed him,” Stevens said. “There are so many Democrats who want to vote for our Democratic nominee. And they’re just being told, ‘Hey, this is a party you don’t belong in, or this is a campaign you don’t belong in.’”

Kelly mocked Stevens on Monday’s episode of her show, telling viewers, “It’s very amusing.”

She added, “I mean, listen, the Democrats made their own bed. I didn’t nominate Haley Stevens. I thought she was bizarre.”

Stevens’ endorsement came after her fiancé, Jason Turkish, lashed out at El-Sayed while Stevens backed him, as well as during an ongoing dispute in which she demanded he disavow a Rebellion PAC ad.

El-Sayed had already distanced himself from the ad, which Stevens claimed has the following messaging: “Jews are responsible for America’s economic woes.” His campaign ultimately asked her to steer clear of any remaining events.

“Who could blame him?” Kelly said, seemingly siding with El-Sayed’s campaign decision.

“Can you imagine if you had won the primary over this ninny and she was like, ‘I’ll go to the unity event as long as you say the following five things exactly as I want you to.’ Fuck off. You lost. That’s what I’d be saying, too,” Kelly added.

“You know, this person should not have been your representative,” Kelly continued. “She should not have been one of your last final candidates.”

The right-wing radio host also took shots at El-Sayed and the Democratic Party following his CBS “60 Minutes” interview.

“The guy’s a problem,” Kelly said. “So they could have gone with him, or they could have gone with a moderate, and they chose as their moderate this nutcase, who is, she’s a phony, and she’s about herself.”
